updates.name: Mark Adams
updates.bio: GIS specialist at Cape Cod National Seashore. A 2017 park news release says he had held that post at the seashore since 1993, concentrating on monitoring coastal change and on documenting how the Outer Cape landscape has shifted over time.

Earlier she was a postdoctoral researcher at Wells NERR and a graduate fellow at Great Bay NERR.

updates.name: Jorge E. Capella
updates.bio: Physical oceanographer who played a central part in founding and developing CARICOOS, building its data management and numerical modeling systems and creating the products and tools its services still rest on. CARICOOS announced his death in September 2025.
updates.evidence: Obituary Notice – Dr. Jorge Capella September 29, 2025 Published by CARICOOS
updates.notes: The CARICOOS obituary notice (2025-09-29) carries its text in an image embedded in the page (read in this run): it announces the passing of Dr. Jorge Capella, physical oceanographer, and credits him with CARICOOS's numerical modeling and data management system. His facility_personnel row (executive-officer, 'Executive Director') looks wrong: the current CARICOOS site (https://www.caricoos.org/board-of-directors) names Julio M. Morell as Executive Director; that row needs a research-batch verdict. Existing homepage https://www.uprm.edu/cima/profesores/ did not respond (connection failed) and is a list page. No ORCID or Scholar link found. Verifier 2026-10-26: evidence replaced with text verbatim from the page (the earlier quote added a parenthetical not on the page); obituary image re-read and supports the bio.

updates.name: Julio M. Morell
updates.bio: Executive director and principal investigator of CARICOOS, the Caribbean regional system within the U.S. Integrated Ocean Observing System, and a research professor in marine sciences at the University of Puerto Rico-Mayagüez. Trained in chemical oceanography, he has studied plankton metabolism, marine pollution, tropical biogeochemistry and greenhouse gases, river plumes and eddies in Caribbean waters, and ocean acidification.
updates.research_interests: plankton metabolism; oil, debris and nutrient pollution; tropical marine biogeochemistry and greenhouse gas cycling; influence of Orinoco and Amazon plumes and mesoscale eddies on Eastern Caribbean waters; ocean acidification and climate
updates.current_title: Executive Director and Principal Investigator, CARICOOS
updates.current_affiliation: CARICOOS; Department of Marine Sciences, University of Puerto Rico-Mayagüez
updates.evidence: Julio Morell serves as CARICOOS Principal Investigator and Executive Director.
updates.notes: Bio from his Ocean Foundation Board of Advisors profile; current role confirmed on the CARICOOS board/officers page. updates.name: Dan Bahauddin
updates.bio: Information manager for Cedar Creek Ecosystem Science Reserve and its LTER program at the University of Minnesota, curating the station scientists' long-term datasets, which reach back more than forty years. On staff since the 1990s, he has also done field and faculty-lab work there, and received the station's Service Award in 2025.

updates.bio: Environmental laboratory manager at the University of New Mexico's Center for Water and the Environment, in Civil, Construction and Environmental Engineering. Earlier, she spent five years as a USDA-ARS physical science technician at the National Soil Erosion Research Laboratory in Indiana, analysing nutrient transport, and has used methods such as colorimetry, gas chromatography and ICP-OES.

updates.name: Charles L. Redman
updates.bio: Emeritus professor in Arizona State University's School of Sustainability, which he led as founding director from 2007 to 2010, after directing ASU's Center for Environmental Studies and the Global Institute of Sustainability. An archaeologist by training, he studies human impacts on environments, urban ecology, sustainable landscapes and fast-urbanizing regions, and has written or co-written 14 books.

updates.name: Mark Watkins
updates.bio: Program manager for Arizona State University's Central Arizona-Phoenix LTER program. Before CAP LTER he coordinated the UGEC (Urbanization and Global Environmental Change) project, and he has worked on renewable energy and sustainability with rural Wisconsin communities and nonprofits. He holds a master's in urban and regional planning from UW-Madison.

updates.name: Nancy B. Grimm
updates.bio: Regents Professor and Virginia M. Ullman Professor of Ecology in Arizona State University's School of Life Sciences. An ecosystem ecologist, she studies how climate change, human activity, resilience and biogeochemistry interact in cities and streams. She was founding director of CAP LTER, now co-leads the NATURA and ESSA networks, and is a National Academy of Sciences member.
